title: Trogir With a Dog 2027: Beaches, Rules, Stays
metaDescription: Planning a trip to Trogir with a dog: dog beaches, old town rules, ferries, accommodation fees, heat, vets and EU pet passport requirements.
content:
## Are Dogs Allowed in Trogir Old Town?

Yes. The old town sits on a small island, and leashed dogs can walk its stone lanes without any special permit. The lanes are narrow and busy from 10:00 to 17:00 in July and August, so a short leash is the practical choice. White limestone paving gets very hot in midsummer. Walk at 07:00–09:00 or after 19:00 and test the surface with your hand. The waterfront promenade (Riva) is the easiest route for a dog, with shade from the buildings in the late afternoon.

The marketing makes Trogir look like a relaxed walking town, but in peak season the old town is too crowded and too hot to enjoy with a large or nervous dog. Treat it as an early-morning and evening visit, not an all-day outing.

## Dog Beaches Near Trogir (Plaža za Pse)

The town's own pebble and concrete bathing spots are not set up for dogs, and some dog-listing sites report no dog beaches inside Trogir proper. The official options are in the surrounding area:

- **Kaštela:** a landscaped beach just east of Trogir that was set up as a dog beach, with the equipment a dog needs for a day out. Leashes are expected when walking among other visitors.
- **Seget Donji:** a marked dog section on the long pebble shore by Hotel Medena, about 5 km west of Trogir.
- **Okrug Gornji (Copacabana), Čiovo:** a two-kilometre gravel beach with a dog-friendly section. Use the marked area only, because the main swimming zones restrict dogs in peak summer.

In Croatia, dogs may generally swim wherever a local ban or sign does not forbid it. Look for the "zabranjeno za pse" (dogs prohibited) sign at the entrance. Hotel and resort beaches set their own rules. Pick up waste and bring fresh water, since pebble beaches offer little shade.

## Restaurants and Cafés

Outdoor terraces in Trogir usually accept dogs, and many waiters bring a water bowl without being asked. Indoor dining rooms are normally off-limits under food-hygiene rules. Ask before sitting down, and choose a table in the shade. Konobas in the old town's side streets tend to be more relaxed than the Riva restaurants, which fill up and have little space under the tables.

## National Parks and Nature

The closest big national park is Krka, roughly 50–60 km from Trogir. Its visitor routes and boat trips are not suited to dogs, and pets are generally not admitted, so check the park's current rules before you drive there. Plitvice has similar restrictions. For hiking with a dog, the Kozjak hills above Kaštela and the coastal paths on Čiovo are easier options. Keep dogs on a leash and avoid midday walks.

## Ferries and Catamarans

Boat day trips to the islands mostly leave from Split, 27 km from Trogir. The rules differ by operator:

- **Jadrolinija ferries:** dogs travel free but must wear a muzzle and stay on a leash. Dogs over 8 kg must stay on the open deck.
- **Jadrolinija catamarans:** only small pets up to 8 kg in a carrier no larger than 45 x 35 x 25 cm are allowed in the lounge. The carrier must stay under the seat or on your lap.
- **Krilo (Kapetan Luka) and TP Line:** onboard kennels cost about €12 per dog on the Split–Hvar route. Confirm the policy when you buy the ticket.

The car-ferry crossing from Split to Supetar on Brač takes about 50 minutes and is the easiest island trip with a larger dog.

## Accommodation Costs for a Dog

Pet fees in the Trogir area typically run €5–20 per night. Some apartments charge a one-off cleaning fee instead, usually €20–50. Many private hosts accept small dogs for free and ask for a deposit or a towel rule. Villas with a fenced garden and a pool are the easiest option for large dogs, but confirm in writing that dogs are allowed in the pool area. Brown Beach House Hotel & Spa and Amadria Park Camping Trogir on Čiovo are among the pet-friendly options in the area. Always confirm the dog policy and any size limit before booking, because rules change by season.

## Summer Heat and Best Months

July and August regularly reach 32–36°C in Dalmatia, and pavement can be far hotter. Short-nosed and heavy-coated breeds should avoid midday outings entirely. The sea is warm enough for swimming from late May to October.

- **April–June:** 18–27°C, quiet beaches, easy restaurant seating. This is the best period for dogs.
- **September–October:** warm sea, fewer visitors, and lower prices at most pet-friendly stays.
- **July–August:** manageable only with early-morning and evening routines, air conditioning, and shade.

Never leave a dog in a parked car, even for a few minutes.

## Vet Basics

Trogir and the neighbouring Kaštela area have several private vet clinics, and Split has the widest emergency cover on the central Dalmatian coast. Save a clinic's number and location before you arrive. Ask your own vet about tick prevention, because ticks are common in dry scrub and gardens. Sandflies, which carry leishmaniasis, are active in summer evenings, so a repellent collar is a sensible precaution. Carry a copy of the vaccination record and your dog's microchip number.

## EU Pet Passport and Entry Rules for Driving In

Croatia applies EU-wide pet travel rules. Dogs need:

1. An ISO 11784/11785 microchip, implanted before or on the same date as the rabies vaccination.
2. A valid rabies vaccination, given at 12 weeks or older, with a 21-day wait before travel.
3. An EU pet passport issued by an authorised vet.

EU-issued passports are accepted at the border. Tapeworm treatment is not required for Croatia. From 22 April 2026, passports held by residents of Great Britain are no longer accepted for entry into the EU. British travellers need an Animal Health Certificate instead, issued within 10 days of entry. Travellers from outside the EU should also check the rules for countries they drive through on the way. Keep the passport in the car, because border and transit checks can ask for it.

## Verdict: How Dog-Friendly Is Trogir?

**Trogir is moderately dog-friendly: 3.5 out of 5.** Leashed dogs are welcome in the old town and on most terraces, and three marked dog beaches are within about 6 km. The weak points are the lack of an official dog beach in the town itself, the summer heat, and the limited rules for catamarans and national parks. It suits small and medium dogs, shoulder-season trips and car travel. Choose a villa or apartment with a garden, and plan beach time away from the old town.

faq.question: Is there a dog beach in Trogir?
faq.answer: There is no official dog beach in Trogir old town itself. The nearest marked dog beaches are in Kaštela, at Seget Donji by Hotel Medena, and in a dog section at Okrug Gornji on Čiovo. Look for the "plaža za pse" sign.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed in Trogir old town and restaurants?
faq.answer: Leashed dogs can walk through the old town. Restaurant terraces usually welcome dogs, but indoor dining rooms generally do not. Ask the staff before you sit down.

faq.question: Can dogs travel on ferries and catamarans from Split?
faq.answer: Yes, with conditions. Jadrolinija carries dogs free of charge, but they must be muzzled and leashed, and dogs over 8 kg must stay on the open deck. On Krilo and TP Line catamarans, onboard kennels cost about €12.

faq.question: How much do hotels and apartments charge for a dog in Trogir?
faq.answer: Pet fees are typically €5–20 per night. Some hosts charge a one-off cleaning fee of €20–50 instead. Confirm size limits and the fee before booking.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia by car?
faq.answer: A dog needs an ISO microchip, a valid rabies vaccination given at least 21 days before travel, and an EU pet passport. Travellers from Great Britain need an Animal Health Certificate, because their EU pet passports are no longer valid for entry.

faq.question: What is the best month to visit Trogir with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June and September are the best months, with warm seas and moderate temperatures. July and August often exceed 32°C, which is too hot for midday walks.

quickAnswer: Trogir is moderately dog-friendly. The old town is open to leashed dogs, and restaurant terraces are usually fine. There is no official dog beach in the town itself, but marked dog beaches exist in Kaštela, Seget Donji and Okrug Gornji. Dogs need an ISO microchip, a rabies vaccination and an EU pet passport. Visit in spring or autumn.
